title: feat(mcp): add device-flow login
author: rekty
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- Adds `startDeviceLogin`, `pollDeviceLogin`, and `whoAmI` to the local stdio MCP
- Keeps the device code and resulting API key inside the MCP process
- Uses the existing form-encoded OAuth device flow with one poll per tool call
- Leaves the hosted stateless MCP unchanged
- Adds focused state-transition and stdio tool-list coverage

Closes #11222

## Verification

- `npm test` in `packages/mcp`
- `node --test worker.test.js` in `apps/mcp`
- Biome check on changed JavaScript files

gist.headline: The hive gets a login button
gist.blurb: The local MCP can now do the civilized thing and sign in through a device code. Your API key stays tucked safely inside the MCP process, where keys prefer to live.
gist.summary: Added startDeviceLogin, pollDeviceLogin, and whoAmI tools to the local stdio MCP, using the existing form-encoded OAuth device flow while keeping device codes and resulting API keys inside the MCP process.
gist.impact: Developers can connect local MCP clients to their Pollinations account through a device-login flow and check the active identity without manually passing API keys around; the hosted stateless MCP remains unchanged.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the local MCP as a cozy retro terminal receiving a small device-code login card, with Polli helping the monitor robot complete the connection. A tiny locked seed jar beside the terminal represents the API key remaining safely inside the local MCP process, while code-plants and flowers make the login flow feel like a healthy new garden path.
